title: Is Pinterest (PINS) Stock a Hidden Winner in the AI-Powered Advertising Boom?

content_html:
Pinterest, Inc. (NYSE:PINS) projected third-quarter 2026 revenue between $1.19 billion and $1.21 billion, surrounding the Wall Street consensus estimate of $1.20 billion. The guided range represents 13% to 15% year-over-year top-line growth, assuming a modest foreign exchange headwind, alongside Q3 Adjusted EBITDA expected between $335 million and $355 million.

For Q2 2026, Pinterest posted revenue of $1.18 billion, up 18% year-over-year (17% in constant currency), driven by an all-time high of 640 million global monthly active users (MAUs), up 11% for its 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit user growth. Global ARPU increased 7% to $1.86, led by the U.S. and Canada at $8.30 (+14%). Adjusted EBITDA reached $311.3 million (26% margin), while GAAP net loss came in at $46.7 million. Free cash flow surged 37% to $269.9 million, supporting over $2 billion in year-to-date share repurchases at an average price of $18.17.

Photo by Souvik Banerjee on Unsplash

Wall Street analysts adjusted price targets following the earnings call. On August 5, Baird's Colin Sebastian raised the firm's price target on PINS to $26 from $24, maintaining a Neutral rating while highlighting solid Q2 results and progress across AI, product, and go-to-market initiatives.

On August 6, Wells Fargo boosted its price target to $31 from $30 with an Overweight rating, noting that while Q2 revenue hit expectations, it benefited from temporary drivers that, as they fade, leave the Q3 outlook slightly below buy-side expectations.

This brings up a key question: Does Pinterest, Inc. (NYSE:PINS)'s Q3 guidance represent a natural normalization after one-off Q2 tailwinds, or is it an early sign of decelerating ad momentum in a crowded social marketplace?

Bull Case

Proponents point to sustained double-digit MAU growth, AI-driven personalizations, and exceptional cash generation. AI models trained on human curation enhance user actionability while lowering serving costs and optimizing ad performance. High free cash flow ($270 million in Q2) funds balance sheet flexibility and continuous share repurchases without relying on external financing.

Bear Case

Bears emphasize volatile GAAP profitability and uneven earnings durability. While global user scale continues expanding, international ARPU remains low ($1.35 in Europe, $0.23 in the Rest of World), requiring a multi-quarter monetization transformation. Moreover, higher infrastructure investments and debt obligations could compress operating leverage if top-line momentum cools off faster than expected.
